The honest comparison

The Urfael assistant, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw: every win and every gap in one table. Urfael wins where it counts for a machine that lives on your desk and acts for you: the smallest blast radius, a flat bill within your plan’s limits, and the ability to prove what it did. We are smaller and newer, and we say so in the same table.

Urfael Assistant, Hermes Agent and OpenClaw, capability by capability
CapabilityUrfael AssistantHermesOpenClaw
No inbound network portnone on the daemon; optional services loopback-onlyvariesgateway/DMs
Ships an attack benchmarkyes, npm run securitynono
Flat-rate cost (no per-token)yes, on your Claude Code plan (its limits and terms apply)nono
Can prove what it did (ledger + seal)yesnono
Live, watchable multi-agent Councilyes (experimental)see their docssee their docs
Undoable coding turns (checkpoint + rewind)yes, auto-checkpoint + reversible rewindnone documentednone documented
Skill hub supply-chain checksscanned + previewed + sha-pinnedexternal standardthird-party registry; see their docs
Proactive memory recall (every turn)retrieves per turnfrozen snapshotagent must search
Generative UI that can't run codesanitized canvas (validator shipped; live rendering not built yet)norenders agent UI
Chat-channel breadth19 (11 native + 8 webhook)many20+
Battle-tested at scalesmall, and we say solargevery large

Where it counts for a machine on your desk: blast radius, cost, provability, and not overstating maturity. OpenClaw and Hermes are genuinely excellent at breadth and scale.

Urfael·Help that lives with you.

Urfael makes friendly AI that lives with you. Urfael Assistant is open source and runs on your own machine today. Uru, a soft helper robot for the home, is at the research stage. Locked down by default. Honest about limits.
